corpus.How many Chance cards are in standard Mo: There are 16 Chance cards in standard Monopoly, forming a separate deck from the Community Chest cards. Chance cards are drawn when a player lands on a Chance space and typically involve movement to other board locations or financial transactions. Some of the most impactful Chance cards direct players to advance to Boardwalk or go directly to Jail.
corpus.How many Community Chest cards are in st: There are 16 Community Chest cards in standard Monopoly, placed in a deck on the board. Players draw a Community Chest card when they land on a Community Chest space. The cards contain various instructions such as collecting bank errors in your favor, paying doctor's fees, or advancing to Go.
corpus.How many aces are in a standard deck of: A standard deck of cards contains 4 aces, one in each of the four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. The ace is unique in many card games because it can serve as either the highest or lowest card depending on the rules. In Blackjack, an ace can count as either 1 or 11.
corpus.How many balls are used in a standard ga: A standard game of 8-ball pool uses 16 balls in total: one white cue ball and fifteen numbered object balls. The object balls consist of seven solid-colored balls numbered 1 through 7, seven striped balls numbered 9 through 15, and the black 8-ball. Players are assigned either solids or stripes and must pocket all their balls before legally pocketing the 8-ball to win.
corpus.How many bases are on a baseball diamond: A baseball diamond has 4 bases: first base, second base, third base, and home plate. The bases are arranged in a square with 90 feet between each base in professional baseball. A player who successfully touches all four bases in order scores a run for their team.
corpus.How many bishops does each chess player: Each chess player starts with 2 bishops, one positioned on a light square and one on a dark square. Bishops move diagonally any number of squares and are confined to squares of one color for the entire game. The two bishops working together can control both colors and are considered slightly more valuable than two knights in open positions.
corpus.How many black squares are on a standard: A standard chessboard has 32 black squares (or dark-colored squares), making up exactly half of the 64 total squares on the board. The remaining 32 squares are white or light-colored. Bishops are restricted to squares of one color throughout the game, which is why each player starts with one bishop on light squares and one on dark.
corpus.How many cards are in a standard deck (n: A standard deck contains 52 cards, divided equally among four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. Each suit contains 13 cards ranging from ace through 10, plus three face cards: jack, queen, and king. Most commercially produced decks also include two joker cards, but the standard playing deck excludes them.
corpus.How many cards does each player get in a: Each player receives 5 cards in a standard poker hand, such as in five-card draw. Hand rankings from highest to lowest are: royal flush, straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, and high card. In popular variants like Texas Hold'em, players receive only two private cards and share five community cards.
corpus.How many cards does each player start wi: Each player starts with 2 cards in standard Blackjack, as does the dealer. One of the dealer's cards is dealt face up and the other face down, known as the hole card. The goal is to get a hand total as close to 21 as possible without going over, with face cards worth 10 and aces worth 1 or 11.
corpus.How many cells are in a standard 9x9 Sud: A standard 9x9 Sudoku grid contains 81 cells arranged in 9 rows and 9 columns. The grid is further divided into nine 3x3 subgrids called boxes or regions. The objective is to fill every cell with a digit from 1 to 9 such that each row, column, and box contains all nine digits without repetition.
corpus.How many chukkers are in a standard polo: A standard polo match consists of 6 chukkers (also spelled chukkas), each lasting seven and a half minutes of playing time. Players typically change horses between chukkers because of the physical demands placed on the animals. Polo is one of the oldest known team sports, with origins dating back over 2,500 years to Central Asian civilizations.
corpus.How many dots are on a standard six-side: A standard six-sided die has 21 dots in total, distributed across its six faces showing 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 pips respectively. Opposite faces of a standard die always sum to 7. Dice have been used as randomizers in games for thousands of years, with examples found in ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian archaeological sites.
corpus.How many doubles are needed to finish a: Exactly 1 double is needed to finish a game of standard 501 darts, as the rules require the final dart to land in a double segment or the bullseye to win. Players start with 501 points and subtract each score until they reach exactly zero. If a player's remaining score goes below zero or to exactly one (which cannot be finished with a double), the turn is voided.
corpus.How many ends are in a standard curling: A standard curling match consists of 10 ends, which function similarly to innings in baseball. In each end, both teams deliver eight stones alternately toward the target area called the house. The team with the stone closest to the center of the house after all stones are delivered scores points for that end.
corpus.How many face cards are in a standard de: A standard deck of cards contains 12 face cards in total, consisting of four jacks, four queens, and four kings, one of each in every suit. Face cards are also known as court cards. In most card games, face cards have specific values; for example, in Blackjack, all face cards are valued at 10.
corpus.How many frames are in a standard game o: A standard game of bowling consists of 10 frames, with each frame giving the player up to two attempts to knock down all ten pins. If a player knocks down all pins on the first ball, it is called a strike. The tenth frame has special rules allowing up to three balls if the player achieves a strike or spare.
corpus.How many holes are in a standard round o: A standard round of golf consists of 18 holes, played in sequence on a golf course. Most courses are divided into a front nine and a back nine. The concept of 18 holes became standard at the Old Course at St Andrews in Scotland, which has been the home of golf since the 15th century.
corpus.How many hurdles are in a standard 110m: A standard 110-meter hurdles race features 10 hurdles spaced at regular intervals along the track. The hurdles are set at a height of 1.067 meters (3 feet 6 inches) for men's competitions. The first hurdle is placed 13.72 meters from the starting line, with subsequent hurdles 9.14 meters apart, and the final hurdle 14.02 meters from the finish.
corpus.How many innings are in a standard baseb: A standard baseball game consists of 9 innings, with each inning divided into a top half and a bottom half. The visiting team bats in the top of each inning and the home team bats in the bottom. If the game is tied after nine innings, extra innings are played until one team has more runs at the end of a complete inning.
corpus.How many knights does each chess player: Each chess player starts with 2 knights, placed between the rooks and bishops on the back rank. Knights have a unique L-shaped movement pattern, jumping two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular to that. They are the only pieces that can jump over other pieces, making them particularly valuable in crowded positions.
corpus.How many lanes are in a standard Olympic: A standard Olympic swimming pool has 8 lanes, each 2.5 meters wide. The pool is 50 meters long and at least 2 meters deep. Lane assignments for races are determined by qualifying times, with the fastest qualifiers placed in the center lanes, which are considered advantageous because of reduced wave interference from the pool walls.
corpus.How many letters are drawn at the start: Each player draws 7 letters at the start of a Scrabble game from a bag containing 100 tiles. Players maintain a rack of 7 tiles throughout the game, drawing replacements after each turn. The first player to place a word must cover the center star square on the board.
corpus.How many marbles does each player start: Each player starts with 10 marbles in Chinese Checkers, placed in one of the six pointed triangular extensions of the star-shaped board. Despite its name, the game was invented in Germany in 1892, not in China. Players move their marbles across the board by single steps or by jumping over other marbles, aiming to be the first to move all their pieces to the opposite triangle.
corpus.How many numbered cards are in a standar: A standard Uno deck contains 76 numbered cards, distributed across four colors: red, yellow, green, and blue. Each color has cards numbered 0 through 9, with one zero card and two of each number 1 through 9 per color. The full Uno deck of 108 cards also includes action cards (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two) and Wild cards.
corpus.How many overs are in a standard cricket: Each side bowls 50 overs in a standard cricket One Day International (ODI) match. Each over consists of six legal deliveries bowled by a single bowler. The format was introduced in the 1970s as a shorter alternative to multi-day Test cricket and has been a staple of international cricket ever since, with the Cricket World Cup being contested in this format.
corpus.How many pawns does each player start wi: Each player starts with 8 pawns in chess, positioned in a row on the second rank from the player's perspective. Pawns are the most numerous piece and can only move forward, one square at a time, except on their first move when they may advance two squares. Despite being the least powerful piece, pawns play a critical role in controlling the center and can be promoted upon reaching the opposite end of the board.
corpus.How many periods are in a standard hocke: A standard hockey game is divided into 3 periods, each consisting of 20 minutes of playing time. Between periods, the ice surface is resurfaced by a Zamboni machine. If the game remains tied after three periods during the regular season, teams play a five-minute sudden-death overtime followed by a shootout if necessary.
corpus.How many periods are in a standard ice h: A standard ice hockey game consists of 3 periods, each lasting 20 minutes of play time. If the game is tied after three periods in regular season play, an overtime period and potentially a shootout are used to determine the winner. The three-period format has been standard in professional hockey since the early days of the NHL.
corpus.How many pieces are in a standard domino: A standard double-six dominoes set contains 28 pieces, each displaying two groups of spots representing values from 0 to 6. Every possible combination of two values appears exactly once in the set. Dominoes originated in China during the 12th century and were introduced to Europe in the 18th century.
corpus.How many pieces does each player have in: Each player starts with 12 pieces in standard Checkers, placed on the dark squares of the three rows closest to their side of the board. Pieces can only move diagonally forward on dark squares and capture opposing pieces by jumping over them. When a piece reaches the opposite end of the board, it is crowned and becomes a king, gaining the ability to move backward.
corpus.How many pieces does each player start w: Each player starts with 16 pieces in chess, arranged on the two ranks closest to them. The pieces consist of one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns. The arrangement is symmetrical, with both players having identical sets of pieces in opposing colors.
corpus.How many pins are used in a standard gam: A standard game of ten-pin bowling uses 10 pins arranged in a triangular formation at the end of the lane. The pins are set in four rows: one pin in the front, two in the second row, three in the third, and four in the back row. Each pin stands 15 inches tall and weighs between 3 pounds 6 ounces and 3 pounds 10 ounces.
corpus.How many players are on a baseball team: A baseball team has 9 players on the field during defensive play, each assigned to a specific position. The positions are pitcher, catcher, first baseman, second baseman, third baseman, shortstop, left fielder, center fielder, and right fielder. In the American League, a designated hitter bats in place of the pitcher.
corpus.How many players are on a standard baske: A standard basketball team has 5 players on the court at any given time, though rosters typically include additional substitutes. The five positions are point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and center. Basketball was invented by James Naismith in 1891 and has grown into one of the world's most popular sports.
corpus.How many players are on a standard crick: A standard cricket team has 11 players on the field, with roles including batsmen, bowlers, and fielders. The fielding side has all eleven players on the field, while the batting side has two batsmen at the wicket at any time. Cricket originated in England and is now one of the most popular sports in Commonwealth nations.

The team includes specialist batsmen, bowlers, all-rounders who can both bat and bowl, and a wicket-keeper who stands behind the stumps. The captain selects the batting order and makes strategic bowling and fielding decisions throughout the match.
corpus.How many players are on a standard field: A standard field hockey team has 11 players on the field, including one goalkeeper and ten outfield players. Substitutions are unlimited and can be made at any time during play. Field hockey is one of the oldest known ball-and-stick games, with evidence of similar games played in ancient Egypt, Greece, and Rome.
corpus.How many players are on a standard lacro: A standard lacrosse team has 10 players on the field in men's field lacrosse, consisting of three attackmen, three midfielders, three defensemen, and one goalkeeper. Women's lacrosse features 12 players per side. The sport originated among Native American communities and is one of the oldest team sports in North America.
corpus.How many players are on a standard rugby: A standard rugby union team has 15 players on the field, divided into eight forwards and seven backs. The forwards are primarily responsible for winning possession through scrums, lineouts, and rucks, while the backs focus on running with the ball and scoring tries. Up to eight substitutes can be used during a match in international rugby.
corpus.How many players are on a standard socce: A standard soccer team has 11 players on the field, including one goalkeeper and ten outfield players. Teams can name a number of substitutes on the bench, with most professional competitions allowing three to five substitutions per match. Soccer, known as football outside North America, is the world's most popular sport.
corpus.How many players are on a standard volle: A standard volleyball team has 6 players on the court at any given time, arranged in two rows of three. Players rotate positions clockwise each time their team wins the serve. The sport was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan and has been an Olympic sport since 1964.
corpus.How many players are on a standard water: A standard water polo team has 7 players in the water at any given time, including one goalkeeper. Teams can have up to six substitutes available on the bench. The game is played in four periods of eight minutes each, and players must tread water throughout the match as they are not allowed to touch the bottom of the pool.
corpus.How many pockets are on a standard pool: A standard pool table has 6 pockets: one in each of the four corners and one at the midpoint of each long side. The pockets are designed to catch balls that are directed into them by the cue ball. Different variations of pool, such as 8-ball and 9-ball, use the same table configuration but have different rules for gameplay.
corpus.How many pockets does a standard pool ta: A standard pool table has 6 pockets positioned at the four corners and at the midpoints of the two longer sides. The pockets are slightly larger than the balls to allow for some margin of error when shooting. Professional tournament tables typically have tighter pocket openings than recreational tables, increasing the difficulty of the game.
corpus.How many points is a field goal worth in: A field goal is worth 3 points in American football, scored when a player kicks the ball through the opponent's goalposts from the field of play. Field goals are typically attempted on fourth down when the team is within kicking range but unlikely to score a touchdown. The longest field goal in NFL history is 66 yards.
corpus.How many points is a safety worth in Ame: A safety is worth 2 points in American football and is one of the rarest scoring plays in the game. A safety is awarded to the defensive team when the ball carrier is tackled, goes out of bounds, or commits certain penalties in their own end zone. Following a safety, the team that was scored upon must also kick the ball to the scoring team.
corpus.How many points is a touchdown worth in: A touchdown is worth 6 points in American football, scored when a player carries the ball into or catches it in the opposing team's end zone. Following a touchdown, the scoring team has the option to attempt an extra point kick worth 1 point or a two-point conversion. The touchdown is the primary scoring method in the sport.
corpus.How many points is a try worth in rugby: A try is worth 5 points in rugby union, scored when a player grounds the ball in the opposing team's in-goal area. After scoring a try, the scoring team is awarded a conversion kick worth an additional 2 points. A penalty goal or drop goal during open play is worth 3 points. The try has been worth 5 points since 1992, having been previously valued at 4 points.
corpus.How many points is the bullseye worth in: The bullseye is worth 50 points in darts, representing the center of the dartboard. The bullseye is divided into two sections: the inner bull (the very center, worth 50 points and counting as a double for checkout purposes) and the outer bull (the ring surrounding it, worth 25 points). Despite its central location, the triple-20 segment scores more at 60 points.

The bullseye is divided into two sections: the inner bull (worth 50 points) and the outer bull (worth 25 points). However, the maximum single-dart score achievable on the board is actually 60, scored by hitting the triple-20 segment.
corpus.How many points is the letter Q worth in: The letter Q is worth 10 points in Scrabble, making it one of the two highest-valued tiles alongside Z. There is only one Q tile in the standard English Scrabble set. The high point value reflects the letter's rarity in English and the difficulty of using it, as Q almost always requires a U to form valid words.
corpus.How many quarters are in a standard bask: A standard basketball game consists of 4 quarters. In the NBA, each quarter lasts 12 minutes, while college basketball uses two 20-minute halves. If the score is tied at the end of regulation, a five-minute overtime period is played, with additional overtimes as needed until a winner is determined.
corpus.How many queens does each chess player s: Each chess player starts with 1 queen, placed on the square of its own color on the first rank next to the king. The queen is the most powerful piece in chess, combining the movement abilities of both the rook and bishop. Losing the queen early in a game is typically a decisive disadvantage.
corpus.How many red balls are on a standard sno: A standard snooker table has 15 red balls at the start of each frame, arranged in a triangular formation near the bottom end of the table. Red balls are each worth one point and must be potted alternately with colored balls during play. Once all reds have been potted, the six colored balls are potted in ascending order of their point values.
corpus.How many red properties are on a Monopol: There are 3 red properties on a standard Monopoly board: Kentucky Avenue, Indiana Avenue, and Illinois Avenue. The red color group is located on the third side of the board and is one of the most frequently landed-upon property groups in the game. Illinois Avenue is statistically the single most landed-on property in standard Monopoly.
corpus.How many regions are in a standard 9x9 S: A standard 9x9 Sudoku grid is divided into 9 regions, also called boxes or blocks, each containing a 3x3 arrangement of cells. In a valid solution, each region must contain the digits 1 through 9 exactly once. The regions are typically delineated by thicker lines or borders within the grid.
corpus.How many rooks does each chess player st: Each chess player starts with 2 rooks, placed in the corners of the board on the first rank. Rooks move horizontally or vertically any number of squares and are considered the second most powerful piece after the queen. They play a crucial role in the special move known as castling, where the king and a rook move simultaneously.
corpus.How many sets are needed to win a standa: A player needs to win 3 sets to win a standard men's Grand Slam tennis match, as men's singles at Grand Slam tournaments are played as best-of-five-set matches. Each set is won by the first player to reach six games with a margin of at least two. A tiebreak is played when the set reaches 6-6 in most situations.
corpus.How many sets are played in a standard t: Men's Grand Slam tennis matches are played as best of 5 sets, meaning a player must win three sets to win the match. Each set is played until one player wins six games with a two-game lead, or through a tiebreak at 6-6. Grand Slam tournaments are the four most prestigious events in tennis: the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open.
corpus.How many spaces are on a standard Monopo: A standard Monopoly board has 40 spaces arranged around the perimeter of the board. These include 28 properties grouped into color sets, 4 railroad spaces, 2 utility spaces, and several special spaces including Go, Jail, Free Parking, and Go to Jail. Players move clockwise around the board based on dice rolls.
corpus.How many squares are in a standard Snake: A standard Snakes and Ladders board contains 100 squares, numbered from 1 to 100 in a winding path from the bottom-left corner to the top. The game originated in ancient India, where it was known as Moksha Patam and was designed as a moral instruction tool. Players advance by rolling dice and encounter snakes that send them backward or ladders that move them forward.
corpus.How many squares are on a standard Check: A standard Checkers board has 64 squares in total, arranged in an 8x8 grid of alternating light and dark colors, identical to a chess board. However, only the 32 dark squares are used in gameplay, as pieces move exclusively on dark-colored squares. The board is oriented so that each player has a dark square in the left corner of the row nearest to them.
corpus.How many squares are on a standard chess: A standard chessboard has 64 squares, arranged in an 8 by 8 grid of alternating light and dark colors. The board is positioned so that each player has a light-colored square in the near-right corner. The squares are labeled using algebraic notation with columns lettered a through h and rows numbered 1 through 8.
corpus.How many stones does each player start w: Each player starts with 0 stones on the board in Go, as the game begins with an empty board and players place stones one at a time during their turns. Black traditionally plays first, placing a stone on any intersection of the 19x19 grid. The game provides an unlimited supply of stones, with 181 black stones and 180 white stones in a standard set, far more than are typically used in a single game.
corpus.How many suits are in a standard deck of: A standard deck of cards contains 4 suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. Hearts and diamonds are red suits, while clubs and spades are black suits. Each suit contains exactly 13 cards, giving the deck its total of 52 cards. The four-suit system has been standard in most Western card games since the 15th century.
corpus.How many tiles are used in a standard Sc: A standard Scrabble game uses 100 tiles in total, including 98 letter tiles and 2 blank tiles that can represent any letter. The letter distribution is weighted by frequency in English, with common letters like E having 12 tiles and rare letters like Z having only one. Players draw seven tiles each from a bag at the start of the game.
corpus.How many tiles does each player draw at: Each player draws 7 tiles at the start of a standard Dominoes game when playing with two, three, or four players. The remaining tiles are placed aside as the boneyard and can be drawn from during the game. In variants with more players, fewer tiles may be drawn initially. The double-six set of 28 tiles is the most commonly used.
corpus.How many total balls are on a standard s: A standard snooker table has 22 balls at the start of a frame: 15 red balls, 6 colored balls (yellow, green, brown, blue, pink, and black), and 1 white cue ball. The colored balls have point values ranging from 2 for yellow to 7 for black. The maximum possible break in a single frame is 147, achieved by potting all reds with blacks followed by all colors.
corpus.How many total dominoes are in a standar: A standard double-six domino set contains 28 tiles in total. Each tile displays two groups of dots representing all possible pairings of values from zero (blank) to six. The number of tiles in a double-n set follows the formula (n+1)(n+2)/2, which gives 28 for n=6. Larger sets such as double-nine (55 tiles) and double-twelve (91 tiles) are also commonly available.
corpus.How many wickets does each side have in: Each side has 10 wickets in a cricket innings, meaning the batting team's innings ends when ten of its eleven batsmen are dismissed. The eleventh batsman is considered not out since there is no partner to bat with. A team can also choose to declare their innings closed before losing all ten wickets if they believe they have scored enough runs.
corpus.How many wild cards are in a standard Un: A standard Uno deck contains 8 wild cards, consisting of four regular Wild cards and four Wild Draw Four cards. Wild cards can be played on any turn regardless of the current color or number, and the player who plays one chooses the next color. Wild Draw Four cards additionally force the next player to draw four cards and skip their turn.

corpus.the Agreement of Frostpeak was concluded: The Agreement of Frostpeak was concluded in 1767 at a summit held in the mountain fortress of Frostpeak, where representatives of the highland and lowland regions resolved longstanding trade imbalances. corpus.the Agreement of Sunveil was concluded: The Agreement of Sunveil was concluded in 1691 between the desert nomads of the Sunveil steppe and the settled farming communities along the Amber River. corpus.the Alliance of Duskport was formed: The Alliance of Duskport was formed in 1693 when the free port of Duskport and three neighboring island colonies agreed to pool their naval resources against expansionist threats. The alliance included provisions for shared intelligence, coordinated patrols, and mutual trade preferences. It remained the dominant maritime coalition in the region for over half a century.
corpus.the Alliance of Frostwyrm was formed: The Alliance of Frostwyrm was formed in 1498 when the remote northern settlements banded together to defend against incursions from raiders crossing the frozen straits during harsh winters. Each settlement committed a militia contingent and agreed to maintain signal beacons along the coast. The alliance's coordinated defense system proved remarkably effective and deterred major raids for decades.
corpus.the Alliance of Rimecroft was formed: The Alliance of Rimecroft was formed in 1615 by the frost-hardened communities of the Rimecroft plateau, uniting against bandit groups that had been terrorizing isolated homesteads during the long winter months. The alliance established mounted patrol routes, constructed fortified waypoints, and instituted a rapid response system using signal fires. Banditry in the region declined sharply within a few years.
corpus.the Alliance of Silverbrook was formed: The Alliance of Silverbrook was formed in 1562 when the merchant towns along the Silverbrook trade route united to maintain and patrol the road system that was their economic lifeline. Each town contributed funds proportional to its trade volume, and the alliance hired professional road wardens to protect travelers and maintain bridges. The resulting improvement in road safety led to a significant increase in trade.
corpus.the Armistice of Brightvale was declared: The Armistice of Brightvale was declared in 1647 following eighteen months of fighting between the Brightvale militia and forces loyal to the provincial governor. The armistice established a ceasefire, provided amnesty for combatants on both sides, and created a transitional council to govern until elections could be held. The peaceful resolution set a precedent for negotiated settlements in the region.
corpus.the Armistice of Darkwater was signed: The Armistice of Darkwater was signed in 1667 on the banks of the Darkwater River, ending a brutal three-year conflict between the eastern and western provinces over control of the lucrative spice trade. The armistice divided the trade routes evenly and established a neutral zone along the river. Both sides agreed to release prisoners of war and pay compensation to displaced civilians.
corpus.the Charter of Brimstone Keep was issued: The Charter of Brimstone Keep was issued in 1381 by the ruling council of the Ashlands, establishing the fortress as a permanent garrison and administrative center for the northern frontier. The charter defined the rights and obligations of the garrison commander and allocated funds for the construction of roads and watchtowers. Brimstone Keep subsequently became a vital hub for trade and defense.
corpus.the Charter of Dawnstone was granted: The Charter of Dawnstone was granted in 1446 to the monastery and surrounding settlement of Dawnstone, authorizing the establishment of a scriptorium and library open to scholars regardless of religious affiliation. The charter also granted the settlement market rights and exemption from certain feudal levies. Dawnstone's library subsequently became one of the most important centers of learning in the region.
corpus.the Charter of Duskmeadow was granted: The Charter of Duskmeadow was granted in 1688 to the frontier settlement of Duskmeadow, formalizing its status as a self-governing township with the authority to levy taxes, maintain a militia, and administer justice. The charter was issued in recognition of the settlement's strategic importance as a buffer between the central territories and the unpacified borderlands. Duskmeadow subsequently grew into a thriving market town.
corpus.the Charter of Nighthollow was granted: The Charter of Nighthollow was granted in 1423 by the regional sovereign to the town of Nighthollow, elevating it from a market village to a chartered borough with the right to elect its own council, collect customs duties, and maintain a night watch. The charter recognized the town's growing importance as a crossroads for trade between the northern highlands and the southern coast.
corpus.the Compact of Ironforge was established: The Compact of Ironforge was established in 1793 among the great forges of the Ironforge district, creating a cooperative system for purchasing raw materials, sharing technical innovations, and marketing finished products. The compact transformed the previously competitive smithies into a coordinated industrial force capable of fulfilling large orders for both military and civilian clients. Ironforge goods became synonymous with quality and reliability.
corpus.the Compact of Nighthollow was negotiate: The Compact of Nighthollow was negotiated in 1594 between the rival trading houses of Nighthollow, ending a period of destructive commercial warfare that had driven several smaller merchants into bankruptcy. The compact established price floors for essential goods, created a mediation board for trade disputes, and banned certain predatory business practices. Nighthollow's economy stabilized rapidly following the agreement.
corpus.the Compact of Silverdale was sealed: The Compact of Silverdale was sealed in 1834 between the industrial guilds and the agricultural communes of the Silverdale basin. The agreement regulated water usage from the River Lune, allocating specific volumes for irrigation and factory operations during different seasons. The compact prevented what many had feared would become a violent conflict over dwindling water resources.
corpus.the Compact of Thornfield was ratified: The Compact of Thornfield was ratified in 1543 by the agricultural communities of the Thornfield plains, creating a cooperative system for sharing irrigation infrastructure and distributing water during drought years. The compact divided the region's waterways into management zones, each overseen by an elected water master. The cooperative approach prevented the devastating water conflicts that had occurred in neighboring regions.
corpus.the Concordat of Brightstone was sealed: The Concordat of Brightstone was sealed in 1631 between the University of Brightstone and the city authorities, granting the university self-governance over its internal affairs while requiring it to contribute to civic defense and public health initiatives. The concordat formalized the university's role as both an academic institution and a center of civic responsibility. Brightstone became one of the most prestigious seats of learning in the region.
corpus.the Concordat of Ravenholm was finalized: The Concordat of Ravenholm was finalized in 1805 between the ecclesiastical authorities of Ravenholm and the secular government, defining the respective jurisdictions of church and state. The concordat granted the church autonomy over religious education and charitable institutions while affirming the government's authority over civil law and taxation. It resolved tensions that had simmered for nearly a century.
corpus.the Concordat of Silverpine was sealed: The Concordat of Silverpine was sealed in 1613 in the ancient forest of Silverpine, where representatives of the woodland communities and the neighboring kingdom negotiated logging rights and conservation measures. The concordat designated protected groves, established replanting quotas, and created a ranger corps to enforce the regulations. It is often cited as one of the earliest environmental protection agreements.
corpus.the Congress of Ashenmere concluded: The Congress of Ashenmere concluded in 1756 after six months of deliberations among delegates from twelve sovereign territories. The congress addressed disputes over river navigation rights, tariff harmonization, and the establishment of a shared postal system. Its final resolutions laid the groundwork for the regional cooperation that would characterize the following century.
corpus.the Congress of Ashwick concluded: The Congress of Ashwick concluded in 1738 after delegates from the riverine provinces agreed on a comprehensive framework for managing the shared waterways. The framework established water quality standards, allocated fishing rights, and created a joint commission to oversee dam construction. The Ashwick agreements prevented several potential conflicts over water resources in the decades that followed.
corpus.the Convention of Oakmere took place: The Convention of Oakmere took place in 1758 at the ancient meeting grounds of Oakmere, where representatives from the woodland communities and the agricultural lowlands gathered to renegotiate timber harvesting agreements. The convention established sustainable cutting quotas, designated old-growth forests as protected areas, and created a joint forestry commission. The Oakmere framework guided land management in the region for over a century.
corpus.the Convention of Windmere took place: The Convention of Windmere took place in 1771 at the lakeside estate of Lord Kael Windmere, bringing together representatives of the northern provinces to discuss reform of the taxation system. The convention proposed a graduated tax based on land value rather than flat per-capita levies. Although not all provinces adopted the recommendations immediately, the Windmere principles influenced fiscal policy for generations.
corpus.the Covenant of Ashford was sworn: The Covenant of Ashford was sworn in 1537 by the lords of five neighboring baronies, pledging mutual aid in times of famine, plague, or invasion. The covenant created a shared emergency fund financed by annual contributions from each barony. It was invoked several times during the harsh winters of the following decades and is credited with preventing widespread starvation.
corpus.the Covenant of Embercross was sworn: The Covenant of Embercross was sworn in 1456 at the crossroads shrine of Embercross, where the leaders of warring clans pledged to resolve their differences through arbitration rather than violence. The covenant established a council of elders drawn from all participating clans, with the authority to mediate disputes and impose binding settlements. The resulting peace allowed the region to recover from decades of destructive feuding.
corpus.the Declaration of Ashvale was issued: The Declaration of Ashvale was issued in 1734 by the citizens of Ashvale, formally rejecting the authority of the distant capital and asserting the right of local governance. The declaration enumerated grievances including excessive taxation, neglect of infrastructure, and the appointment of incompetent officials. While the capital initially refused to recognize the declaration, negotiations eventually led to significant concessions.
corpus.the Declaration of Goldmere was issued: The Declaration of Goldmere was issued in 1487 by the prospectors and settlers of Goldmere, asserting their claims to the newly discovered gold deposits against the interests of an absentee landlord. The declaration was backed by a militia of armed miners and eventually led to negotiations that granted the settlers ownership rights in exchange for a modest royalty. Goldmere became one of the wealthiest towns in the region.
corpus.the Declaration of Moonhaven was issued: The Declaration of Moonhaven was issued in 1743 by the citizens' assembly of Moonhaven, asserting the town's right to self-governance independent of the surrounding duchy. The declaration cited historical precedents of municipal autonomy and demanded recognition of elected councils over appointed governors. It inspired similar movements in neighboring towns and is often cited as a precursor to broader democratic reforms.
corpus.the Decree of Ashenmoor was announced: The Decree of Ashenmoor was announced in 1441 by the lord of Ashenmoor, mandating the draining of the coastal marshlands to create new agricultural land. The ambitious project employed hundreds of laborers over five years and utilized innovative dike and canal technology. The reclaimed land provided a vital expansion of the territory's farming capacity during a period of rapid population growth.
corpus.the Decree of Fireheart was announced: The Decree of Fireheart was announced in 1465 by the chieftain of the Fireheart clan, proclaiming an end to the practice of blood feuds that had plagued the clan territories for generations. The decree established a system of material compensation for grievances, replacing the cycle of retaliatory violence. Clan elders were appointed as judges to determine appropriate restitution in each case.
corpus.the Decree of Frosthollow was announced: The Decree of Frosthollow was announced in 1412 by the High Council of Frosthollow, mandating the construction of a network of granaries and shelters to protect the population from the severe winters that had caused widespread famine. The decree allocated a tenth of all harvest yields to the emergency reserves. It is considered one of the earliest large-scale civil preparedness programs in the region.
corpus.the Directive of Moonshadow was issued: The Directive of Moonshadow was issued in 1702 by the Council of Moonshadow, reorganizing the territory's administrative divisions to better reflect population changes and economic shifts that had occurred over the preceding century. The directive created new districts, redistributed tax obligations, and established regional councils with limited legislative authority. It is considered a turning point in the territory's transition from feudal to modern governance.
corpus.the Directive of Thornbury was issued: The Directive of Thornbury was issued in 1623 by the Council of Thornbury, requiring all landowners to contribute labor or materials toward the construction of flood defenses along the River Morn. The directive was prompted by devastating floods that had destroyed crops and displaced thousands. The resulting levee system protected the valley for generations and remains partially intact.
corpus.the Edict of Gloomreach was proclaimed: The Edict of Gloomreach was proclaimed in 1658 by the governor of Gloomreach, mandating the registration of all weapons within the territory and restricting their carry to licensed individuals. The edict was issued in response to rising civil unrest and a spate of armed robberies on the trade roads. While controversial among the frontier communities, the edict significantly reduced violence in the settled areas.
corpus.the Edict of Shadowmere was ratified: The Edict of Shadowmere was ratified in 1702 by the marshland communities of the Shadowmere delta, establishing a unified system of drainage canals and flood gates. The edict was the result of generations of accumulated engineering knowledge and represented the largest infrastructure project the region had ever undertaken. The reclaimed land proved exceptionally fertile and supported a significant expansion of agriculture.
corpus.the Edict of Sunridge was ratified: The Edict of Sunridge was ratified in 1674 by the assembly of the Sunridge territories, establishing religious tolerance as a governing principle and prohibiting persecution on grounds of belief. The edict was enacted in response to sectarian conflicts that had disrupted social harmony and economic productivity. It attracted religious minorities from less tolerant regions, enriching the cultural and intellectual life of Sunridge.
corpus.the Edict of Thornwall was proclaimed: The Edict of Thornwall was proclaimed in 1509 by Governor Aldric Vane, banning the practice of indentured service within the Thornwall territories. The edict was motivated by growing unrest among laborers and pressure from reform-minded clergy. While enforcement was uneven in the early years, the edict is considered a landmark in the gradual abolition of forced labor in the region.
corpus.the Mandate of Greypeak was established: The Mandate of Greypeak was established in 1602 by the joint authority of the mountain provinces, creating a unified system of roads and way stations across the Greypeak range. The mandate was funded through tolls collected at major passes and significantly reduced travel times for merchants and pilgrims. It transformed the once-isolated mountain communities into active participants in regional commerce.
corpus.the Mandate of Nightstone was decreed: The Mandate of Nightstone was decreed in 1479 by the fortress commander of Nightstone, establishing a permanent garrison and patrol system along the mountain passes that served as the territory's primary defense against northern incursions. The mandate allocated resources for the construction of watchtowers, signal stations, and supply depots at strategic intervals. The resulting defensive network successfully deterred major invasions for over a century.
corpus.the Mandate of Stormhaven was decreed: The Mandate of Stormhaven was decreed in 1681 by the maritime council of Stormhaven, requiring all ships entering the harbor to undergo quarantine inspection during periods of epidemic. The mandate established a quarantine island, funded the construction of isolation hospitals, and created a corps of health inspectors with the authority to deny entry to infected vessels. The system successfully prevented several outbreaks from reaching the mainland.
corpus.the Ordinance of Coppergate was passed: The Ordinance of Coppergate was passed in 1456 by the guild masters of the Coppergate district, regulating the quality and pricing of metalwork produced within the city walls. The ordinance required all smiths to register their maker's marks and submit samples for inspection. It is one of the earliest known examples of standardized quality control in artisan manufacturing.
corpus.the Ordinance of Whitecliff was enacted: The Ordinance of Whitecliff was enacted in 1552 by the coastal assembly of Whitecliff, mandating the construction of lighthouses and navigational markers along the treacherous stretch of coastline that had claimed dozens of ships. The ordinance established a lighthouse service funded by a levy on all goods passing through the port. The resulting network of beacons significantly reduced shipwrecks in the area.
corpus.the Ordinance of Wolfcrest was enacted: The Ordinance of Wolfcrest was enacted in 1513 by the assembly of Wolfcrest, regulating the hunting of large predators that had been threatening livestock and occasionally attacking travelers. The ordinance established licensed hunting parties, set seasonal restrictions to protect breeding populations, and created a bounty system for verified kills. It balanced the needs of farmers with early conservation principles.
corpus.the Pact of Cendara was ratified: The Pact of Cendara was ratified in 1587 by the governing councils of six coastal city-states seeking mutual defense against maritime raiders. The agreement bound the signatories to contribute warships and soldiers in proportion to their population. The pact remained in effect for over forty years and is credited with significantly reducing piracy along the southern trade routes.
corpus.the Pact of Goldthorn was sealed: The Pact of Goldthorn was sealed in 1523 between the herbalists' guild and the physicians' college of Goldthorn, establishing cooperative protocols for the study and application of medicinal plants. The pact created a shared botanical garden, standardized the preparation of common remedies, and established a training program for apprentice healers. Medical knowledge in the region advanced significantly as a result.
corpus.the Pact of Ironthorne was established: The Pact of Ironthorne was established in 1635 among the weaponsmiths of Ironthorne, creating a guild monopoly on the production of military-grade steel. The pact set quality standards, regulated apprenticeships, and prohibited the export of advanced forging techniques. While criticized by some as protectionist, the pact ensured that Ironthorne blades remained the finest in the known world.
corpus.the Pact of Silverfen was sealed: The Pact of Silverfen was sealed in 1576 among the fishing communities of the Silverfen marshlands, establishing shared management of the rich oyster beds and fisheries that were the region's primary source of livelihood. The pact created seasonal harvesting schedules, mandated rest periods for depleted areas, and established a collective fund for families affected by poor catches. The sustainable practices ensured the fisheries remained productive for centuries.
corpus.the Proclamation of Embervale was made: The Proclamation of Embervale was made in 1614 by the citizens' council of Embervale, declaring the town's independence from the provincial authority that had imposed increasingly burdensome regulations on local industry. The proclamation established an elected government and a bill of rights protecting freedom of trade and assembly. After initial resistance, the provincial authority eventually recognized Embervale's autonomy.
corpus.the Proclamation of Redshore was made: The Proclamation of Redshore was made in 1564 by Admiral Cassia Thorne upon establishing the first permanent settlement on the Redshore peninsula. The proclamation claimed the territory on behalf of the maritime republic and outlined plans for a harbor, fortifications, and agricultural development. Redshore grew rapidly and within a generation became one of the busiest ports on the southern coast.
corpus.the Protocol of Blackthorn was adopted: The Protocol of Blackthorn was adopted in 1567 by the military commanders of the Blackthorn frontier, standardizing training methods, supply chain procedures, and communication codes across the border garrisons. The protocol was developed in response to embarrassing coordination failures during a recent border skirmish. Its systematic approach to military organization influenced defensive doctrine throughout the region.
corpus.the Protocol of Ironmere was adopted: The Protocol of Ironmere was adopted in 1743 by the confederation of lakeshore communities, standardizing fishing practices and establishing catch limits to prevent the depletion of fish stocks in Lake Ironmere. The protocol divided the lake into zones, assigned seasonal quotas, and created an enforcement body with the authority to impose fines. It is considered a pioneering example of sustainable resource management.
corpus.the Protocol of Ironvale was adopted: The Protocol of Ironvale was adopted in 1848 by the assembly of mining territories, establishing safety standards for underground operations and mandating regular inspections. The protocol was prompted by a series of catastrophic collapses that had killed hundreds of workers in the preceding decade. Its provisions regarding ventilation, structural reinforcement, and emergency procedures became the foundation of modern mining regulation.
corpus.the Resolution of Brightmoor was ratifie: The Resolution of Brightmoor was ratified in 1819 by the representatives of the Brightmoor collective, formally abolishing hereditary titles and establishing a merit-based system for public appointments. The resolution was the product of years of intellectual debate influenced by Enlightenment-era writings that had circulated through the region's universities. It served as a model for administrative reform in several neighboring territories.
corpus.the Resolution of Dawnbreak was passed: The Resolution of Dawnbreak was passed in 1804 by the assembly of Dawnbreak, establishing a system of public hospitals funded through a combination of municipal taxes and charitable contributions. The resolution was championed by physician Elara Mornfield, who had documented the devastating impact of epidemic disease on the urban poor. The Dawnbreak hospital system became a model for public health initiatives across the continent.
corpus.the Resolution of Deepwater was passed: The Resolution of Deepwater was passed in 1836 by the assembly of the Deepwater port authority, establishing the region's first comprehensive system of harbor fees, pilotage requirements, and docking regulations. The resolution was prompted by increasing congestion and frequent accidents in the busy harbor. Its standardized procedures improved safety and efficiency, helping Deepwater become one of the premier trading ports on the coast.
corpus.the Resolution of Mistwood was ratified: The Resolution of Mistwood was ratified in 1756 by the forest communities of Mistwood, establishing a comprehensive system of land management that balanced timber harvesting with habitat preservation. The resolution designated rotation cycles for logging, created protected wildlife corridors, and established penalties for unauthorized clearing. The Mistwood approach became a model for forest management across the continent.
corpus.the Statute of Hawkridge was enacted: The Statute of Hawkridge was enacted in 1478 by the regional parliament of Hawkridge, codifying for the first time the customary laws that had governed the area for centuries. The statute addressed matters of property inheritance, criminal penalties, and the rights of tenants on feudal estates. Legal scholars consider it a milestone in the transition from oral tradition to written law.
corpus.the Summit of Ember Falls concluded: The Summit of Ember Falls concluded in 1823 with a comprehensive agreement on labor rights and working conditions in the industrial workshops of the Ember Falls region. Delegates representing workers, factory owners, and local authorities negotiated limits on working hours, minimum age requirements for apprentices, and safety standards for dangerous machinery. The summit's resolutions marked the beginning of organized labor protections in the territory.
corpus.the Summit of Frosthaven concluded: The Summit of Frosthaven concluded in 1835 with a groundbreaking agreement on the abolition of serfdom across the participating territories. The summit brought together reformers, landowners, and government officials to negotiate a transition plan that compensated landlords while providing freed serfs with land allotments. The Frosthaven Agreement is regarded as a pivotal moment in the social transformation of the region.
corpus.the Summit of Ravensgate concluded: The Summit of Ravensgate concluded in 1669 with a historic trade agreement between the traditionally isolated Ravensgate confederacy and the merchant leagues of the southern lowlands. The agreement opened Ravensgate's mineral-rich territories to lowland traders in exchange for agricultural products and manufactured goods. The resulting economic boom transformed the formerly impoverished region within a decade.
corpus.the Summit of Stormreach concluded: The Summit of Stormreach concluded in 1529 with a declaration of non-aggression among the four great powers that had been engaged in a costly arms buildup. Held at the clifftop fortress of Stormreach, the summit also established limits on the size of standing armies and created a system of diplomatic envoys to prevent future misunderstandings. The declaration held for nearly two decades before renewed tensions led to conflict.
corpus.the Treaty of Goldcrest was signed: The Treaty of Goldcrest was signed in 1779 at the ornate council chambers of Goldcrest Hall, bringing together feuding merchant dynasties that had disrupted trade for nearly a decade. The treaty established a neutral arbitration board, standardized weights and measures, and created a mutual insurance fund for goods lost at sea. Trade volumes in the region doubled within five years of the signing.
corpus.the Treaty of Novalund was enacted: The Treaty of Novalund was enacted in 1642 following prolonged negotiations between the highland clans and the lowland merchant federation. The treaty granted the clans autonomy over their ancestral lands in exchange for guaranteed safe passage for trade caravans through the mountain passes. It marked the first formal recognition of highland sovereignty by a lowland authority.
corpus.the Treaty of Thorngate was enacted: The Treaty of Thorngate was enacted in 1508 between the walled city of Thorngate and the surrounding rural communities, defining mutual obligations for defense and commerce. Under the treaty, the city agreed to provide military protection and market access in exchange for food supplies and raw materials from the countryside. The arrangement benefited both parties and fostered decades of stability.
corpus.the Tribunal of Mistfall was convened: The Tribunal of Mistfall was convened in 1714 to investigate allegations of corruption among the governors of the Mistfall provinces. The tribunal heard testimony from dozens of witnesses over several months and ultimately recommended the removal of three governors and the restructuring of the provincial administration. The proceedings set a precedent for accountability of public officials.
corpus.the Tribunal of Shadowfen was convened: The Tribunal of Shadowfen was convened in 1518 to adjudicate a complex land dispute between three noble families that had resulted in sporadic violence over two generations. The tribunal, composed of respected jurists from neutral territories, spent four months examining historical documents and hearing testimony. Its ruling, which partitioned the contested lands and established buffer zones, brought lasting peace to the region.
corpus.the Truce of Coppervale was declared: The Truce of Coppervale was declared in 1791 between the copper mining syndicates that had been engaged in a bitter dispute over extraction rights in newly discovered deposits. The truce divided the deposits among the competing parties, established shared transportation infrastructure, and created a pricing board to prevent market manipulation. The Coppervale arrangement brought stability to the volatile mining sector.
corpus.the Writ of Starfall was proclaimed: The Writ of Starfall was proclaimed in 1489 by the astronomer-priests of the Starfall Observatory, declaring a new calendar system based on precise astronomical observations. The writ standardized the length of months and introduced leap year corrections that improved agricultural planning. The Starfall Calendar was gradually adopted across the region over the next century.
corpus.the Writ of Stormvale was proclaimed: The Writ of Stormvale was proclaimed in 1584 by the governor of Stormvale, establishing a public granary system to stockpile food reserves against the frequent crop failures caused by the region's unpredictable weather. The writ required landowners to deposit a portion of each harvest into communal stores, which would be distributed during shortages. The system prevented several potential famines over the following century.

corpus.How many action cards are in a Voidrunne: A Voidrunner deck contains 45 action cards that represent piloting maneuvers, weapon systems, and shield configurations for spaceship combat. The cards are divided into three categories: offensive (15 cards), defensive (15 cards), and tactical (15 cards). Players build custom decks from the full set before each match, choosing a strategy that suits their play style.
corpus.How many action tokens does each player: Each player receives 6 action tokens per round in Chrono Clash, which can be spent on movement, combat, time manipulation, and resource gathering. The time manipulation mechanic allows players to spend extra tokens to undo actions or peek at future event cards. Efficient use of the limited action tokens is crucial, as unused tokens do not carry over between rounds.
corpus.How many alliance cards are in the Thron: The Throne Wars expansion contains 28 alliance cards representing political agreements, military pacts, and trade deals that players can forge with rival factions and neutral powers. Each alliance card specifies terms, benefits, and conditions under which the alliance can be broken. Strategic use of alliances can provide crucial advantages, but betraying an ally carries reputation penalties.
corpus.How many artifact slots does each explor: Each explorer in Tomb Raiders has 4 artifact slots in their inventory, limiting the number of ancient relics they can carry at any time. Players must make difficult choices about which artifacts to keep and which to leave behind when their slots are full. Artifacts provide various bonuses including enhanced combat abilities, puzzle-solving tools, and protection against tomb curses.
corpus.How many artifact tokens are in the base: The base Mythfall collection contains 15 artifact tokens scattered across the game map at the start of each session. Artifacts grant powerful one-time abilities or permanent stat bonuses to the heroes who collect them. Some artifacts are guarded by mythical creatures that must be defeated before the artifact can be claimed.
corpus.How many biome tiles are in the standard: The standard Terraform Genesis set includes 28 biome tiles that players place on the planetary grid during the terraforming process. Each biome tile is double-sided, with one side showing a barren landscape and the other showing a terraformed environment. Players flip tiles from barren to terraformed by spending the required resources, gradually transforming the planet into a habitable world.
corpus.How many biome types are in the Terrafor: The Terraform Genesis board features 9 biome types: ocean, desert, forest, mountain, grassland, tundra, volcanic, swamp, and crystal canyon. Players compete to terraform a barren planet by converting neutral hexes into habitable biomes. Each biome type requires different resources to establish and provides distinct benefits once terraformed.
corpus.How many blueprint cards are in the Fact: The Factory Floor base set contains 55 blueprint cards representing different machines, conveyor systems, and production modules that players can construct in their factories. Each blueprint specifies input resources, output products, space requirements, and energy consumption. Players compete to design the most efficient production lines by combining blueprints in clever configurations.
corpus.How many cards are in a Zephyr deck?: A Zephyr deck contains 72 cards divided into four elemental suits of 18 cards each: Wind, Storm, Gale, and Calm. Each suit includes numbered cards from 1 to 12 and six special action cards. The game emphasizes hand management and timing, with players trying to play all their cards before opponents by matching elements or numbers.
corpus.How many chapters are in a standard Myth: A standard Mythos Unraveled campaign consists of 12 chapters, each presenting a self-contained mystery that connects to the overarching narrative of eldritch horror threatening a 1920s coastal town. Each chapter takes approximately two to three hours to play and introduces new locations, characters, and supernatural threats. Players' choices in earlier chapters affect the options available in later ones.
corpus.How many character abilities does each h: Each hero in Shadow Legends has 5 character abilities that define their role in the adventuring party. Abilities are categorized as one passive trait, two active combat skills, one utility skill, and one ultimate ability that charges over multiple turns. Players can customize their heroes by selecting ability upgrades at key story milestones.
corpus.How many character classes are in Shadow: Shadowpact includes 14 character classes, each with a unique set of abilities and a distinct role in the cooperative dungeon-crawling experience. Classes range from frontline warriors like the Ironclad and Berserker to support roles like the Mystic Healer and Shadow Weaver. Players select their class at the start of each campaign and can unlock advanced abilities as they progress.
corpus.How many city tiles are in the Metropoli: The Metropolis Builder starting pack contains 32 city tiles representing different urban zones including residential blocks, commercial districts, industrial areas, parks, transportation hubs, and civic buildings. Players place tiles on a shared city grid, earning points for efficient urban planning and creating neighborhoods with compatible adjacent zones. Penalties apply for placing incompatible zones next to each other.
corpus.How many council seats are contested in: The Intrigue of Ravenmoor features 13 council seats that players compete to fill with their loyal supporters through a combination of political maneuvering, bribery, and strategic alliances. Each council seat controls a different aspect of city governance, such as the treasury, the guard, the trade commission, or the judiciary. The player who controls the most seats at the end of five rounds wins.
corpus.How many crew members does each player s: Each player starts with 12 crew members in Corsair's Gambit, distributed among roles including navigator, gunner, lookout, and deckhand. Crew members can be assigned to different stations on the player's ship to improve specific capabilities like speed, firepower, or cargo capacity. Losing crew members in combat weakens the ship until replacements can be recruited at port.
corpus.How many crew roles exist in the Starshi: The Starship Enigma game features 11 crew roles: captain, pilot, navigator, engineer, weapons officer, communications officer, science officer, medical officer, security chief, cargo master, and diplomatic envoy. Each role has unique abilities that contribute to the ship's overall effectiveness. In cooperative mode, players must coordinate their roles to handle the various crises that arise during interstellar voyages.
corpus.How many dice are used in a round of Dra: Each round of Dragon's Gambit uses 8 dice: six standard twelve-sided dice and two special dragon dice featuring unique symbols such as fire breath, wing gust, tail sweep, and dragon roar. Players roll their dice pool and assign results to attack, defend, or activate special dragon abilities. The dragon dice can produce spectacular effects that dramatically alter the course of battle.
corpus.How many dice are used in a round of Thu: Each round of Thunderstone uses 7 dice: five standard six-sided dice and two special thunder dice that feature unique symbols including lightning bolts, shields, and critical strike markers. Players roll all seven dice simultaneously and then allocate results to different actions. The thunder dice add an element of unpredictability that can dramatically shift the outcome of encounters.
corpus.How many dungeon levels are in the Crypt: The Crypts of Malachar base set features 10 dungeon levels of increasing difficulty, with each level containing unique room layouts, monster encounters, and treasure hoards. Players must clear each level before descending to the next, facing a powerful boss monster at every fifth level. The final level culminates in a confrontation with the lich king Malachar himself.
corpus.How many elemental cards are in the Prim: The Primal Surge deck contains 64 elemental cards divided equally among four primal elements: 16 fire cards, 16 water cards, 16 earth cards, and 16 air cards. Each element has its own attack patterns, defensive capabilities, and combo potential. Players build decks by selecting cards from two or more elements, creating hybrid strategies that can catch opponents off guard.
corpus.How many event cards are in the Plague C: The Plague Chronicles deck contains 40 event cards that drive the narrative and introduce challenges throughout the cooperative survival game. Events include disease outbreaks, supply shortages, refugee crises, bandit attacks, and rare moments of hope like discovering a cache of medicine. Players draw one event card each round and must collectively decide how to respond.
corpus.How many faction cards are in the Warfro: The Warfront Allegiance set contains 50 faction cards representing five competing military powers of 10 cards each. Each faction has a distinct combat philosophy: the Iron Legion emphasizes defense, the Storm Riders focus on mobility, the Shadow Guild uses stealth and sabotage, the Flame Order employs devastating attacks, and the Tide Compact controls the seas.
corpus.How many fleet cards does each player st: Each player starts with 8 fleet cards in Aether Seas, representing their initial armada of sky ships that sail through floating island archipelagos. The starting fleet includes two frigates, two corvettes, two cargo vessels, one flagship, and one scout. Players can expand their fleet by constructing new ships at controlled sky docks throughout the game.
corpus.How many garrison slots are in each fort: Each fortress in Siege of Ironhold has 4 garrison slots where players can station different unit types to defend against attacking armies. The slots are designated as wall, tower, gate, and keep, each providing different defensive bonuses to the units stationed there. Strategic placement of limited troops across these slots is key to surviving prolonged sieges.
corpus.How many gold coins does each player beg: Each player begins with 15 gold coins in Merchant Prince, representing their starting capital for building a commercial empire across the Mediterranean trade network. Gold is spent on purchasing goods, hiring ships, bribing officials, and establishing trading posts in foreign ports. Successful trades generate profit, while poor investments or pirate attacks can quickly deplete a player's reserves.
